claims_extracted.claim: PUP defines a standard internetwork packet intended to cross multiple interconnected packet-switching networks.
PUP packet-level communication is end-to-end and higher reliability is the responsibility of endpoint protocols.
The standard PUP has a 20-byte header, network/host/socket source and destination addressing, up to 532 content bytes, and a checksum.
The memo specifies encapsulation over Ethernet, ARPANET and low-speed synchronous links, with gateways decapsulating, routing and re-encapsulating PUPs.

notes: Earlier 1975 PUP specifications require a separate source record to reconstruct protocol changes. Do not back-project the 1978 document onto 1973 Ethernet experiments without corroboration.
